title: marginal-cost-sensitivity-quickchecks-and-finance-queries
content:
Purpose
- Quick internal review notes capturing small exploratory sensitivity checks we ran on the Optimize cost model (marginal token-level costs) and a short list of open questions for Finance sign-off.
- Not intended as the canonical model doc; this is a rapid-fire sanity checkpoint after pulling updated cloud invoices + dedicated capacity quotes.

Context and impetus
- Trigger: Updated GCP and AWS GPU list pricing (NVIDIA H100 + A100), and a late change to reserved capacity amortization schedules from Finance (longer useful life).
- We re-ran the marginal cost sheet (sheet:optimize/marginal-cost-q1-2026-v3) with: new GPU per-hour, updated utilization assumptions, and two new batching profiles (low-latency, throughput-optimized).
- Objective: identify any single-assumption swings >10% in unit token cost and surface items Finance needs to confirm before we publish updated recommendations.

Data sources used (versions)
- Cloud pricing: aws-gpu-pricing-2025-11.csv (pulled 2025-11-01) — used for baseline on A100p/RTX families.
- Cloud pricing: gcp-h100-list-2026-01.csv (pulled 2026-01-15) — used for H100 pricing and preemptible rates.
- Invoices: infra-invoices-2025-Q4-export.xlsx (extracted 2026-01-28) — validated historical effective rates after discounts.
- Dedicated quotes: sales/dedicated-quotes-2026-v2.pdf (received 2026-02-12) — used for reserved capacity amortization inputs.
- Usage traces: prod-token-histograms-2025-12.parquet (sampled) — token length and concurrency distributions.
- Cost model sheet: optimize/marginal-cost-q1-2026-v3 (master).

Key calibration steps performed
- Step 1: Align hourly GPU cost with invoice effective rates. For AWS we used blended hourly rate = invoice_total_gpu_charge / invoice_gpu_hours. This differs from list price by ~8% for Q4 due to credits.
- Step 2: Adjust amortization life for dedicated rigs from 36 -> 48 months per Finance guidance (impact: increases monthly capex add-back to unit cost by ~15% relative to prior model).
- Step 3: Recalibrate utilization assumption. Two scenarios: conservative (70% util) and optimistic (90% util) based on observed cluster metrics.
- Step 4: Add preemption fallback cost for spot/HPA mixes: assume 15% task restart overhead (IO + token re-generation) when using preemptible capacity.
- Step 5: Incorporate KV cache hit-rate sensitivity: base = 25% prefix hits, test range 10%–50%. Cache has outsized effect on LLM serving costs for long-context models.

Quick sensitivity findings (one-line summaries)
- GPU hourly rate +/-10% -> unit token cost shifts ~7% (linear).
- Utilization 70% -> 90% range produces ~20% swing in unit cost for dedicated pools.
- Amortization life 36->48 months -> unit cost reduction ~12% for dedicated capex-heavy scenarios.
- KV cache hit-rate 10% -> 50% -> unit cost reduction up to ~18% for long-context generation workload.
- Batching profile (low-latency vs throughput) affects costs non-linearly: throughput batching reduces unit cost by up to 30% at high concurrency but increases tail latency; pick per-route defaults.
- Quantization (fp16 -> int8-ish) yields 8%–22% cost reduction depending on model sensitivity and throughput profile; conservatively assume 10% until QA passes.

Open/ambiguous items for Finance confirmation
- Effective cloud discounts: our blended invoice-derived hourly was lower than list price; Finance, can you confirm whether Q4 credits are recurring or one-off? If one-off, we should not bake them into baseline. (jira:FIN-2107)
- Depreciation schedule: Finance suggested 48 months for dedicated rigs — confirm capital policy for equipment (useful life) and whether we should include residual resale value assumptions.
- Support and SRE overhead allocation: current model applies a 12% ops allocation on top of infra costs. Finance, please confirm if we should switch to a FTE-based allocation model for FY26.
- Marketplace fees and network egress: some customer usage in APAC uses partner transit with per-GB fees. Need a small add-on per-embedding call; Finance to confirm average egress rate to use.

Risks and model fragility callouts
- Small errors in token distribution sampling bias the amortized cost dramatically for prompt-heavy (short token) vs generation-heavy (long token) workloads. We should add per-route token histograms.
- Overnight price changes for H100 (volatile) can flip hosted API margins quickly. Recommend weekly price-check automation and a small price-protection buffer in recommendations.
- Preemption/restart costs poorly instrumented: we estimated 15% overhead from synthetic runs; still needs production validation (SRE).

Proposed conservative defaults for public recommendations (so we can publish without Finance sign-off delays)
- Use invoice-blended GPU hourly but floor to 90% of list price (avoids over-optimism).
- Utilization default = 75% for dedicated pools (documented and defensible).
- KV cache hit-rate default = 25% for streaming/chat workloads, 40% for rerank/embedding-heavy workloads (callouts in the sheet).
- Quantization discount = 10% unit cost until model-specific QA confirms larger wins.

Action items and owners (short list)
- Finance (Carlos Rivera): confirm whether Q4 credits are recurring and final depreciation policy for rigs (due 2026-03-05).
- SRE (Liam O'Rourke): run 2-week targeted preemption experiments on a staging pool and return measured restart overhead (due 2026-03-12).
- Applied ML/Product (Priya Menon + Ethan Chen): validate quantization quality/regression for top-5 production models and publish per-model discount recommendations (due 2026-03-19).
- Product (Maya Patel): update public Optimize recommendation doc with conservative defaults and flag 'assumptions' section for customers (due 2026-03-10).

Short-term recommendations for finance sign-off page
- We should ask Finance to sign off specifically on: (A) depreciation life, (B) whether to include recurring invoice credits, (C) FTE vs percentage ops allocation. With those three confirmed we can lock the FY26 public unit economics.

Quick appendix notes (scratch calculations)
- Example: baseline GPU blended = $6.75/hr -> amortized add-on per token at 75% util = $0.0000023/token (assuming 2.5 tokens/sec average across requests). Small changes in tokens/sec estimate cause big proportional change.
- Batching scenario: throughput batching (slot size 64) vs latency (slot size 1) shows 0.28x unit cost at peak concurrency for throughput; but p95 latency moves from 120ms -> 650ms.

Unresolved questions for discussion
- Should we publish separate public SKUs for latency-optimized vs cost-optimized routes? Operational complexity increases, but mapping makes economics transparent.
- Do we include a standard 5% pricing buffer for hosted API to protect against rapid infra price increases?

Notes to self / rough brainstorming (informal)
- Could automate weekly cloud price pulls + a GitHub action that triggers a recalibration job; model outputs opened as PR for Finance to ack.
- Consider adding a "risk-adjusted unit cost" column with a stress test (30% higher GPU cost, 20% lower cache hit) for enterprise-facing docs.

Bottom line (short)
- No single input caused >30% surprise in our runs, but a combination (lower utilization + shorter amortization + lower cache hit) can breach our tolerance. Need Finance confirmation on credits and depreciation before final publish.

----
Revision history
- 2025-11-04: initial exploratory run (v1).
- 2026-01-20: rebase on updated GCP H100 list (v2).
- 2026-02-28: added amortization change and detailed action items after finance sync (this doc).

End of notes.
